title: Folded cascode OTA
description: A single-ended folded cascode, drawn at rest: the input pair steers current into two folding nodes, and a cascoded branch on each side carries what is left of each folding source's current down to a cascoded NMOS current mirror, whose output side is the high-impedance output. The feedback the application closes around it holds the output at $V_{out,dc}$, and the two inputs sit apart by whatever offset that takes. The mirror is the low-voltage kind: its two devices share a gate, and that gate is the diode side's output node — where the diode side's PMOS and NMOS cascodes meet — so that node sits one mirror $V_{GS}$ above ground while the output sits at $V_{out,dc}$. The two sides therefore do not sit at the same voltages, and every device below the tail is drawn on its own side. It is the branch-current bookkeeping showcase. The tail is drawn the way the circuit sets it: only the bias reference is programmed, with $I_{tail}$; the tail device shares its gate and width and delivers the programmed current less the mirror's drain-voltage error, and the pair's two transistors are one width, each carrying its own share of what the tail delivers. The folding current sources are mirror outputs of a PMOS bias line derived from the same reference, as one reference programs a whole chip's bias: an NMOS mirror output on the reference's gate wire, $K_p$ times its width, sinks its current from a diode-connected PMOS, and the output side's folding source sits on that diode's gate at $K_b$ times its width. The PMOS gate wire's level is solved, by a one-unknown search on that level, so that the NMOS device's drain voltage is the diode's, the one current both carry. The folding source's current, about $K_b K_p I_{tail}$, is read from the table at its own drain voltage, and its partner on the diode side shares its gate and width, so its current is read the same way at its own. On each side the cascoded branch carries the fold current, the folding source's current less the pair transistor's: on the output side that is $I_{fold}$; on the diode side it is what the mirror's diode side carries, and the mirror's output side shares its gate and width, so what it pulls from the output is read from the table at its own drain voltage. The share is solved by a design constraint so that the currents at the output node balance, and the difference between the two pair transistors' gate-source voltages is reported as the systematic offset. The fold current is a real design knob, set by the two ratios: it must be at least the input device's current, so that when slewing steers the whole tail current into one folding node the branch there never starves, but the folding current sources add input-referred noise, so more fold current trades noise for slew headroom. Gain is the pair's transconductance times the folded-cascode output resistance, read on the output side; unlike the telescopic it separates the input CM range from the output swing, at the cost of the extra branch current and its noise. The stack is parameterized by its NODES: the tail node is solved by a design constraint so the produced $CM_{in}$ equals $CM_{dc}$; the gates of the cascodes are bias lines both sides share, each a diode-connected device at a low inversion level carrying its own programmed current — an NMOS one strong-inversion $V_{GS}$ above ground for the NMOS cascodes, a PMOS one the same below the supply for the PMOS cascodes. The output side's folding node $V_{fold}$ and mirror-drain node $V_c$ are solved under those gates by design constraints, and so are the diode side's two nodes, so wherever the design is held the nodes move with the devices; the knobs that place them are the bias diodes' inversion levels. Every bias gate is drawn, so the only ports are the two input gates, which the application drives. Every device $V_{DS}$ is a subtraction between adjacent nodes and every source-above-bulk device carries its true body bias, so the drops close each branch by construction.

params.name: Av_target
params.note: DC gain target: 300 (about 50 dB) is what one cascoded stage reaches at these lengths without gain boosting, about 8-bit static accuracy in unity feedback, the class of a switched-capacitor integrator or sample-and-hold of moderate precision. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: GBW_target
params.note: unity-gain bandwidth target into the 2 pF load: a single-stage OTA with a 20 uA tail at moderate inversion lands in the high single-digit megahertz. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: SR_target
params.note: slew-rate target: the tail current into the 2 pF load; 5 V/us moves a 0.5 V step in 100 ns, the range of a low-power single-stage OTA at a 20 uA tail. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget. The folding current sources are the fold's noise price: with each device's noise read from the tables, the equation lands near 42.5 nV/rtHz on a sky130 tt realization with the PMOS devices on the pfet table, over this budget and well above a telescopic at the same gm. No simulated floor exists for this topology

params.name: vos_target
params.note: input offset budget, 1 sigma; the output mirror's spread referred through the fold puts the total near 6.0 mV on a sky130 tt realization, with the pair, the folding sources and the mirror all at 1 um

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low end — checked exactly by the cm-lo range end at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.92-1.64 V on sky130 tt at the shipped choices: below it the tail device leaves saturation, and above it the tail node runs out of its search range). The range end checks the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high end — its ENDPOINT checked by the cm-hi range end the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; the NMOS-side nodes climb to it and the folding node descends to it. The PMOS and NMOS cascodes meet at a high-impedance output that nothing on this sheet holds; the feedback the application closes around the amplifier holds it here

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the pair's source. Solved rather than set: searched between min and max (the range it is searched in, not slider bounds) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc

params.name: V_fold
params.note: the output side's folding node: the output-side pair transistor's drain, its folding source's drain and its PMOS cascode's source in one. Solved, not set: the cascode's gate is the PMOS cascode bias line, so this is the node that sits the cascode's own gate-source voltage above it; gm_id_cbp is the knob that moves it. That pair transistor's vds is V_fold - V_tail, the folding source's is VDD - V_fold, and the PMOS cascode's is V_fold - V_out_dc — by construction. Searched between min and max, inside the range the wiring puts the node in; the stored value is never read

params.name: V_c
params.note: the output side's NMOS internal node: the mirror output device's drain and the output-side NMOS cascode's source. Solved, not set: the cascode's gate is the NMOS cascode bias line, so this is the node that hangs the cascode's own gate-source voltage under it; gm_id_cbn is the knob that moves it. That mirror device's vds is V_c and its cascode's is V_out_dc - V_c, by construction. The diode side's node under the same gate sits a few millivolts lower, because that cascode's drain is the mirror node, so the mirror's diode side needs this node a little above its knee. Searched between min and max, inside the range the wiring puts the node in; the stored value is never read

params.name: V_fold_r
params.note: the diode side's folding node: the diode-side pair transistor's drain, its folding source's drain and the diode-side PMOS cascode's source. Solved, not set: the two PMOS cascodes share one gate, the PMOS cascode bias line, so this is the node that sits the diode-side cascode's own gate-source voltage above it. Searched between min and max; the stored value is never read

params.name: V_c_r
params.note: the diode side's NMOS internal node: the mirror diode side's drain and the diode-side NMOS cascode's source. Solved, not set: the two NMOS cascodes share one gate, the NMOS cascode bias line, so this is the node that hangs the diode-side cascode's own gate-source voltage under it. Searched between min and max; the stored value is never read

params.name: out_share
params.note: the share of the tail current the pair's output-side transistor carries at rest — solved, not set. The output is a high-impedance node that the feedback around the amplifier holds at V_out_dc, so in the resting circuit the fold current the output-side PMOS cascode brings down is exactly the current the mirror's output side pulls: the engine searches for the share at which the two are equal, the current law at the output node. The diode-side transistor carries the rest, so the two add up to what the tail delivers by construction. It is searched between 0.01 and 0.99; the stored value is never read

params.name: V_bp
params.note: the PMOS bias line: the gate wire the folding sources share, which is the PMOS bias diode's drain and the drain of the NMOS mirror output that sinks its current. Solved, not set: that NMOS device's current depends on its drain voltage, the diode's gate-source voltage depends on that current, and the wire sits one diode drop below the supply, so the engine searches for the level at which the two agree. It is searched between ground and the supply, the range the wiring puts the wire in; the stored value is never read

params.name: avt
params.note: Pelgrom A_VT

params.name: abeta
params.note: Pelgrom A_beta

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis. Read both sides of each PMOS pair from the same table: the gate voltage they share is passed in that table's convention

params.name: I_tail
params.note: the current the bias reference is programmed to — the one tail current on this sheet that is typed. The tail device mirrors it 1:1 through the shared gate and delivers it less the mirror's drain-voltage error (the tail node sits below the reference's diode drop); the input pair's transconductance and the slew rate are computed from what is delivered, not from this number

params.name: K_p
params.note: width ratio of the NMOS mirror output that feeds the PMOS bias diode to the bias reference: the PMOS bias line carries about K_p times the programmed current, which it costs in supply current

params.name: K_b
params.note: width ratio of the output side's folding source to the PMOS bias diode: the folding sources carry about K_b times the bias line's current, so the folding current is about K_b K_p I_tail. The fold current I_fold, that less the output-side pair transistor's current, must stay at least that current (slew headroom vs current-source noise)

params.name: gm_id_cbn
params.note: inversion level of the NMOS cascode bias diode. Its gate-source voltage is the NMOS cascodes' gate, so a lower gm/ID raises the gate and V_c under it, which gives the mirror more drain voltage and the output less swing

params.name: I_cbn
params.note: the current the NMOS cascode bias diode is programmed to. A diode at a given inversion level sits at one gate-source voltage whatever its current, so this sets only its width

params.name: gm_id_cbp
params.note: inversion level of the PMOS cascode bias diode. Its drop below the supply is the PMOS cascodes' gate, so a lower gm/ID lowers the gate and raises V_fold above it, which gives the pair more drain voltage and the folding sources less

params.name: I_cbp
params.note: the current the PMOS cascode bias diode is programmed to; like I_cbn it sets only the diode's width

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion, set on the output-side transistor; its partner copies its width and carries the rest of the tail current. Sets gm per current and the input-referred noise

params.name: gm_id_casc
params.note: cascode-device inversion, set on the two output-side cascodes; the diode-side cascodes copy their widths. Higher gm/ID lifts cascode gain but costs vdsat headroom

params.name: gm_id_cs
params.note: current-source and mirror inversion, set on the output side's folding source and on the mirror's diode side, and inherited by their partners through the shared gates: lower gm/ID adds less noise and offset

params.name: L_in
params.note: length of the input pair: at 1 um its area takes the pair's share of the offset under budget with the pair carrying half of what the tail delivers

params.name: L_cs
params.note: length of the folding current sources and of the output mirror. Their output resistance sets the gain and the mirror's area the larger part of the offset, so they are long — 1 um, with the input pair at the same length: at half a micron, pair and current sources both, the design misses its offset budget at the low end of its common-mode range on a sky130 tt realization

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: inversion level of the bias reference, which the tail device inherits through the shared gate: a higher V* costs headroom at the tail node

params.name: L_tail
params.note: length of the bias reference and of the tail device, which mirror at one length: longer shrinks the mirror's drain-voltage error

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device, on the bias reference's gate at the reference's width: a 1:1 mirror of the programmed current, with $V_{tail}$ as its drain-source voltage. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the reference sits at its own diode drop and this device at $V_{tail}$, so it delivers the programmed current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. It has to stay saturated, and it leaves saturation when $V_{tail}$ falls below its own $V_{dsat}$, which is what sets the low end of the usable common-mode range.

params.name: W_t
params.note: the bias reference's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_t
params.note: the bias reference's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

params.name: vds_t
params.note: the tail node

doc.title: Input-pair device, output side
doc.description: The pair transistor on the output side's folding node, sized at its share of what the tail delivers; it evaluates before the folding branch so the branch can read its current. It publishes its width, which its partner on the diode side copies, and its gate-source voltage, which differs from its partner's by the input offset that holds the output where it is.

doc.title: Folding current source (PMOS), output side
doc.description: The output side's top current source, a mirror output of the PMOS bias diode: on the diode's gate wire at K_b times its width and at its length, so it copies the diode's current density and its current is read off the table at its own drain voltage rather than typed. It feeds the output side's folding node. Its ro (cascoded) sets the PMOS-side output resistance, and it adds input-referred noise. It publishes its width and its gate voltage, which its partner on the diode side copies.

params.name: W_p
params.note: K_b times the PMOS bias diode's width

params.name: vgs_p
params.note: the PMOS bias diode's gate voltage — the bias line the two share, in the sign convention of the diode's table

doc.title: PMOS cascode (folded branch), output side
doc.description: Cascodes the output side's folding current source; carries the fold current I_fold, the output side's folding-source current less the output-side pair transistor's. Its av0 sets the PMOS-side cascode boost. It publishes its width, which the diode-side cascode copies.

doc.title: Folding current source (PMOS), diode side
doc.description: The diode side's top current source, on the output-side source's gate at its width; feeds the diode side's folding node. Its current is read off the table at its own drain voltage rather than typed: wherever the diode side's folding node does not sit where the output side's does, it differs from the output side's.

params.name: W_p
params.note: the output-side source's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_p
params.note: the output-side source's gate voltage — the bias line the two share, in the sign convention of that source's table

doc.title: Input-pair device, diode side
doc.description: The pair transistor on the diode side's folding node: the output-side transistor's width, carrying the rest of what the tail delivers. A matched pair is one width, so its width is copied, and its current is given, which makes this a width-and-current sizing: the table is inverted at that current density for the gate-source voltage it takes. Its body bias is the tail node, like its partner's. Wherever its current or its drain differs from its partner's, so does its gate-source voltage, and that difference is the input offset the sheet reports.

params.name: W_i
params.note: the output-side transistor's width — a matched pair

params.name: I_side
params.note: what the tail delivers less the output-side transistor's share

params.name: vds_i
params.note: from the tail node up to the diode side's folding node

doc.title: NMOS mirror, diode side
doc.description: The diode side of the bottom mirror, carrying the diode side's fold current — its folding source's current less the diode-side pair transistor's. Its gate is the diode side's output node, where the two diode-side cascodes meet, so that node sits one $V_{GS}$ above ground, and its width and gate voltage are what the mirror's output side copies. Its drain is the diode side's NMOS internal node.

doc.title: NMOS mirror, output side
doc.description: The output side of the bottom mirror, on the diode side's gate at the diode side's width; its ro (cascoded by the output-side NMOS cascode) sets the NMOS-side output resistance, and it adds input-referred noise. Its drain is V_c, so its current is read off the table at that drain voltage rather than typed, and the share the output-side pair transistor carries follows it.

params.name: W_m
params.note: the diode side's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_m
params.note: the diode side's gate voltage — the gate the two share

doc.title: NMOS cascode (output branch), output side
doc.description: Cascodes the mirror's output side and carries its current. Its av0 sets the NMOS-side cascode boost. It publishes its width, which the diode-side cascode copies.

doc.title: NMOS cascode, diode side
doc.description: The diode side's NMOS cascode: the output-side cascode's width, on the gate the two share, carrying the diode side's fold current, which it reads from the mirror's diode side below it. Its drain is the diode side's output node — the mirror's gate, one mirror $V_{GS}$ above ground — rather than the output, so its gate-source voltage is read off the table at its own current and drain voltage, and the node under it is solved so that this voltage hangs it under the shared gate.

params.name: W_c
params.note: the output-side cascode's width

doc.title: PMOS cascode (folded branch), diode side
doc.description: The diode side's PMOS cascode: the output-side cascode's width, on the gate the two share, carrying the diode side's fold current, which it reads from the mirror's diode side in the same branch. Its drain is the diode side's output node, the mirror's gate, so its drain-source voltage is what is left between the diode side's folding node and one mirror $V_{GS}$ above ground; the folding node is solved so that its gate-source voltage sits it above the shared gate. Its body bias is VDD less that node (the PMOS tables' vsb axis carries that magnitude).

params.name: W_c
params.note: the output-side cascode's width

equations.name: CM_in
equations.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting: the tail node plus the mean of the two pair transistors' gate-source voltages, the level the two inputs sit about. It rises monotonically with the tail node, so the design constraint that places the tail node from CM_dc is a well-posed one-unknown search

equations.name: tail_headroom
equations.note: how far the tail node sits above the tail device's saturation voltage — exact, because the tail node is the variable rather than something inferred from a common mode

equations.name: I_fold
equations.note: the output side's fold current: what the output side's folding source carries minus the output-side pair transistor's current

equations.name: gm_pair
equations.note: the pair's transconductance into the output node. Each pair transistor turns half the differential input into current, which its folding branch carries on unchanged: the diode-side half reaches the output through the bottom mirror, whose current gain is its output device's $g_m$ over its diode device's, and the output-side half arrives directly. It is either transistor's own $g_m$ where the two sides sit at the same levels

equations.name: Rout_p
equations.note: PMOS side: the output side's folding current source ro boosted by its PMOS cascode's gain

equations.name: Rout_n
equations.note: NMOS side: the mirror output device's ro boosted by the output-side NMOS cascode's gain

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: the two cascoded sides in parallel. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this equation is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: Av
equations.note: folded-cascode gain: the pair's transconductance into the output resistance, both sides of which are read at the output node

equations.name: SR
equations.note: the whole tail current steered into the load — the current the tail device delivers, not the number the reference is programmed to

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: both pair transistors plus both folding sources and both mirror devices, each at its own density: a pair transistor's noise is in series with its own input; a folding source's or a mirror device's is a current at its folding node or at the output, referred back through the pair's transconductance. The diode side's two, its folding source and the mirror's diode device, reach the output through the bottom mirror, as the diode side's half of the signal does in gm_pair, so each is multiplied by the mirror's gain gm_nmir/gm_nmir_r (which leaves the diode device at gm_nmir). Each side is read separately because the two sides sit at different voltages; the folding sources are the price of the fold

equations.name: vos
equations.expr: sqrt((pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, inr__gm/inr__id)^2 + pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, in__gm/in__id)^2)/2 + (pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, nmir_r__W, L_cs, gm_id_cs)*nmir_r__gm/gm_pair)^2)
equations.note: random offset, 1 sigma: the input pair's offset plus the output mirror's offset referred through the pair's transconductance. Each pair transistor contributes half of a matched pair's variance at its own gm/ID — the two share a width but not a current. The mirror pair is read at its diode side, whose width the output side copies

equations.name: vos_sys
equations.note: input-referred systematic offset — the difference of the two pair transistors' gate-source voltages at rest, read directly: the input offset the feedback holding the output at $V_{out,dc}$ has to apply. The mirror's two sides sit at different drain voltages and so do the two folding sources, so the two fold currents differ, and the pair's two transistors carry different shares to make the output balance. Reported only; no check reads it

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single pair transistor, as the mean of the two, which differ a little because their currents do. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No check reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — both folding current sources, which are the only devices of the amplifier itself sitting on the supply rail, each at the current it delivers. The tail current is not a third branch: it is drawn down THROUGH those sources and returned to ground by the tail device, so their sum already contains it and equals the other way of writing the same number, what the tail delivers plus the two fold currents. The bias branches — the reference that programs the tail, the PMOS bias line derived from it and the two cascode bias diodes — are shared bias infrastructure and are not counted here. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no check reads it

checks.note: the folded branch must carry at least what the input device does, so that when slewing steers the whole tail current into one folding node the branch there does not starve

reads each device's thermal noise from the table where the table carries it, and the gamma = 1 estimate where it does not; it stays advisory because a sheet cannot know which table it will be evaluated on, and the simulator owns noise sign-off
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below; the cm-lo/cm-hi range ends check the held design at the ENDS of the range, and the CM_dc sweep shows the whole landscape

operatingRange.name: cm-lo
operatingRange.note: the claimed low end, checked exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo on the design this run produced — its own tail-node solve over its full range, every device held at the geometry it was sized to — and every physical and spec check must hold there

operatingRange.name: cm-hi
operatingRange.note: the claimed high end, checked the same way. The range ends check the ENDPOINTS; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
